content: Far and away the best prize that life has to offer is the chance to work hard at work worth doing.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Theodore Roosevelt's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
